A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs present the same SPO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and four-page supplementary material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original SD-1.5 and SDXL evaluations, ablations, and human preference results in Tables 1–9 and Figure 6, alongside qualitative examples.

after.justification: v4 retains the original model evaluations, ablations, human preference study, and qualitative results reported in v3.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 retain the same candidate sampling, step-aware preference model, random next-step selection, SPO objective, and multi-step extension for SDXL.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Pick-a-Pic data coverage, GenEval evaluation, PartiPrompts/HPSV2 human-study prompts, and Glyph-ByT5-SDXL graphic-design examples. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout Tables 1–3 and Figure 6. Table 1 retains vanilla SDXL, Diffusion-DPO, and MAPO; Table 2 retains vanilla SD-1.5, DDPO, D3PO, and Diffusion-DPO.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 500 Pick-a-Pic validation prompts, 553 GenEval prompts, 10-annotator/300-pair human-study protocol, evaluation metrics, and training and inference settings.

E4.justification: Tables 4–9 retain identical analyses of initialization, preference-model variants, candidate count, inner steps, timestep range, and win-lose selection. The supplementary preference-disagreement case studies also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and user-study percentages. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and Figure 6 are identical. For example, SPO-SDXL retains an aesthetic score of 6.364 in Table 1 and GenEval overall score of 55.20 in Table 3. Qualitative images and findings also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the preference-order assumption under added noise, and the adaptive-normalization formulas in supplementary Section 2 are unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical scientific claims about extracting aesthetic preferences from generic data, improving image aesthetics, and reducing training cost.

C2.justification: Sections 4.6 and 5.3–5.4 retain the same mechanism explanations and limitations, including the stochastic-step requirement, limited image-text alignment benefits, and reliance on crowdsourced aesthetic preferences.

D1.justification: The code/model access statement, hyperparameters, LoRA configuration, sampler settings, GPU and training-time information, and supplementary SPM implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 35 references and the same related-work discussion and positioning. Reference 21 shifts fully onto page 9; it is not added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 removes the acknowledgment of Liang Zheng's ARC Future Fellowship FT240100820 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and main and supplementary section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are minor typesetting differences and reference reflow on PDF pages 9–10 following the acknowledgment removal. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–11 retain their content and organization without redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the same method, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations, including the supplementary material. Removing the brief ARC acknowledgment loses funding attribution, while the remaining edits concern the version stamp and typesetting. These limited changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
